en.exec.goalRunHint: Off by default: when checked, the run arms dsh built-in /goal with the task objective, so the session keeps working automatic continuation rounds until the agent marks the goal complete, and the board settles the execution only when that goal really ends. Unchecked: one plain turn.
en.exec.hint: Applied when the task runs: the workspace decides where the execution session lands; the agent preset composes the session (tool face and prompt sections); the permission is applied through the /permission command. Blank inherits the deployment default.
en.exec.reasoning.hint.inherit: Leave it empty to follow the model or Host default.
en.exec.reasoning.hint.noEfforts: This model offers no selectable reasoning effort, so the model or Host default always applies.
en.exec.reasoning.hint.pickModel: Pin a model first, then choose its reasoning effort.
en.exec.reasoning.hint.unknownModel: The current roster cannot confirm this model's effort levels; the stored value is kept as it is.
en.exec.reuseSessionHint: When on, later runs continue in the previous session (when that session is idle and still exists) instead of starting a new conversation each time; the pinned permission and model above are re-applied on every reuse.
en.exec.skipVerificationHint: Off by default: when checked, a goal-form run of this task no longer gates update_goal on a passing acceptance, and the execution record is marked as skipped. It applies only to executions started afterwards, and means nothing while the board-wide acceptance switch is off.
en.exec.teamRun: Run with an Agent Team (Lead + teammates)
en.exec.teamRunAutoHint: Once a subtask is created or linked, the parent task turns on Agent Team execution automatically (you can switch it off at any time).
en.exec.teamRunHint: On: running this task starts one Lead session and spawns a teammate per subtask inside it, working in parallel (a subtask permission pin does not apply). Off: every member gets its own independent session.
en.exec.teamRunUnavailable: This deployment serves no Agent Teams service, so team runs cannot be enabled.

en.new.subtaskInherit: Execution settings left unset inherit the parent (workspace, mode, permission, model); override any of them here.

en.settings.announceToAgent: Announce the task board to agents
en.settings.announceToAgentHint: On: every agent system prompt includes a note about this board. Off: no announcement; agents learn about the board only when you mention it.
en.settings.cardDefaultModeHint: Blank pins nothing: a new card keeps following the deployment default preset. A target resolves as the explicit choice in the new-task dialog, then the value carried over from the source card or parent, then this default; a subtask keeps what its parent already pinned.
en.settings.cardDefaultModelHint: Blank is the host default (agent-default-model). An explicit choice in the dialog wins over the value carried over from the source card or parent, which wins over this default; a caller that pins a model of its own borrows no default reasoning level.
en.settings.cardDefaultPermissionHint: Blank sets nothing (the session default applies). A default above the session permission baseline is still only a prefill: the card still needs a human confirmation before it may run. A subtask never carries its parent permission; this default fills in only where the parent pinned none.
en.settings.cardDefaultsCardHint: What the new-task dialog opens with: agent preset, permission, model and reasoning effort. Blank sets nothing, so creating a card behaves exactly as it does unconfigured. They are only prefills and change no existing meaning, and every new card stays editable; the default reasoning effort applies only while a card ends up on the configured default model.
en.settings.description: Task orchestration, agent announcement and goal acceptance.
en.settings.enabledCardHint: Master switch, announcement, sleep protection and subtask depth.
en.settings.enabledHint: When off, the sidebar entry and board view are hidden and the task_board_* agent tools are unregistered; while on, any session can read and drive the board, its subtasks and its schedules through those tools.
en.settings.goalRunGlobal: Global: run tasks with dsh native /goal
en.settings.goalRunGlobalDisabledTaskOption: The global native /goal switch is off: the task-level option can still be checked or cleared, but it has no effect right now and the preference you save is never rewritten; turning the global switch back on applies it. This execution runs one plain turn and performs no goal acceptance.
en.settings.goalRunGlobalHint: Off by default. While off, every task runs one plain turn and never calls dsh built-in /goal; a run uses native /goal only when this is on AND the task-level option is checked (see the task option below). The task-level checkbox always stays operable and this switch never rewrites it: the master switch only decides whether that choice takes effect. The switch is frozen when an execution starts, so it only affects runs opened afterwards.
en.settings.goalVerificationCardHint: The switch, the judge model and the criteria threshold.
en.settings.goalVerificationEffortFallback: The selected reasoning effort {requested} is not supported by the target model; it falls back to {resolved}.
en.settings.goalVerificationEffortFallbackN: The selected reasoning effort {requested} is not supported by the target model; it falls back to that model default level (not sent explicitly).
en.settings.goalVerificationEffortHint: Blank inherits the host default level. A level the target model does not declare is never sent blindly: the acceptance falls back to that model own default level, and the fallback is reported below.
en.settings.goalVerificationHint: On by default: a task executed in goal form must pass one acceptance before update_goal may mark it complete (the three coding criteria, aimed at engineering tasks, a 0.65 threshold, two rounds per criterion with the A/B slots swapped, and the work must beat the empty-work baseline). A first failure returns the total, the per-criterion scores and the located findings to the fixing agent, and one execution may accept at most twice; a second failure fails that execution. It affects only this board goal-form executions, never plain chat and never a task pinned to goalRun: false. Every acceptance really calls the judge model and spends quota.
en.settings.goalVerificationModelHint: Blank inherits the host: the default route of the host model catalog, never the card pinned execution model.
en.settings.goalVerificationModelInvalid: The configured judge model is not a provider/model route; the host default is used instead.
en.settings.goalVerificationResolvedNoEffor: Reasoning effort: not sent explicitly (the model default)
en.settings.goalVerificationResolvedPreset: Rubric: coding (Specification Adherence / Output Match / Error Signal Detection), threshold {threshold}
en.settings.goalVerificationRouteMissing: The host serves no model catalog, so no judge route resolves: with acceptance on, a goal completion claim is refused and recorded as an acceptance anomaly.
en.settings.invalidNumber: Enter a number, or leave blank to use the default.
en.settings.maxSubtaskDepthHint: Default 1: a task may carry one level of subtasks, and a subtask cannot create or link further subtasks. Maximum 3. Running a task also runs its whole subtask tree concurrently, and every extra level opens more sessions per run.
en.settings.notExposed: This DSH version does not expose this plugin's settings namespace to the configuration page, so the form is unavailable. Edit ~/.dsh/settings.yaml directly, or add the namespace to the Host settings allowlist and restart.
en.settings.powerBoundary: This may use more battery. Lid close, manual sleep, hibernation, shutdown, low-battery actions, and enterprise policy are outside the guarantee; an already sleeping computer is not woken.
en.settings.powerStatus: Platform: {platform}; protection: {phase}; running sessions: {running}; enabled schedules: {schedules}
en.settings.preventIdleSleepHint: Off by default. When enabled, the Host prevents idle system sleep while any DSH session runs, any schedule is enabled, or session state is not yet known. The display may still turn off.
en.settings.runBehaviorCardHint: The global native /goal switch (master control, off by default).
en.settings.runLaunchWidthHint: Default 3. A run opens its whole subtree, but only this many members create their session and queue their prompt at the same time; the rest wait their turn. Every member still starts, entering the running column in batches. The default comes from this repository's measured guidance for heavy implementation subagents (at most three). Range 1 to 16: a larger width starts runs sooner and costs the Host more memory and swap. Edited during a run, it bounds the launches that have not been admitted yet.
en.settings.saveFailed: The deployment did not accept these values; they were left for you to correct.
en.settings.sessionPollSecondsHint: Default 5. The Host reads the DSH session roster only while the board has something to reconcile: a running card or an open execution. With neither it stops polling and never re-scans the persisted session directory. Range 1 to 300 seconds: a shorter interval settles runs sooner and costs the Host more.
en.settings.spendBudgetTokensHint: Default 0 means no gate: behavior is exactly what it was before this setting existed, with no ledger read and no counting. With a positive cap, once today's measured spend reaches it a manual run or re-run is refused and the caller sees that message as the refusal, while a due schedule writes the reason to the scheduler error and skips that occurrence without spending a planned run — raising the cap, or the local day rolling over, lets the next trigger run as usual. The unit is tokens rather than money: the usage ledger prices only DeepSeek's own routes and stays 0 on every other route. Today's spend is that ledger's local-date bucket summed over input, cache read/write and output, the same measure the usage panel shows.

en.tags.deleteConfirm: Remove the label "{name}" from {count} task(s)? Its execution hint is removed with it; the tasks themselves are unaffected.
en.tags.hint: Labels feed the board filter and the card badges. Renaming writes to every card (merging into a label that already exists), and deleting removes the label from every task including archived ones; the tasks themselves are untouched.
